From 3aafe923987cb4a15e16f03c6185ed4b6a78ca00 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jonathan Cameron <Jonathan.Cameron@huawei.com>
Date: Sun, 8 May 2022 18:56:55 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] iio: gyro: fxas210002c: Fix alignment for DMA safety
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

____cacheline_aligned is an insufficient guarantee for non-coherent DMA
on platforms with 128 byte cachelines above L1.  Switch to the updated
IIO_DMA_MINALIGN definition.

Updated the comment to 'may' require.

Fixes: a0701b6263ae ("iio: gyro: add core driver for fxas21002c")
Signed-off-by: Jonathan Cameron <Jonathan.Cameron@huawei.com>
Reviewed-by: Rui Miguel Silva <rui.silva@linaro.org>
Acked-by: Nuno Sá <nuno.sa@analog.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220508175712.647246-76-jic23@kernel.org

diff --git a/drivers/iio/gyro/fxas21002c_core.c b/drivers/iio/gyro/fxas21002c_core.c
index 0923fd793492..a36d71d9e3ea 100644
--- a/drivers/iio/gyro/fxas21002c_core.c
+++ b/drivers/iio/gyro/fxas21002c_core.c
@@ -150,10 +150,10 @@ struct fxas21002c_data {
 	struct regulator *vddio;
 
 	/*
-	 * DMA (thus cache coherency maintenance) requires the
-	 * transfer buffers to live in their own cache lines.
+	 * DMA (thus cache coherency maintenance) may require the
+	 * transfer buffers live in their own cache lines.
 	 */
-	s16 buffer[8] ____cacheline_aligned;
+	s16 buffer[8] __aligned(IIO_DMA_MINALIGN);
 };
 
 enum fxas21002c_channel_index {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/iio/gyro/fxas21002c_core.c`**
   - The alignment of the `buffer` array in the `fxas21002c_data` structure has been changed from using `____cacheline_aligned` to `__aligned(IIO_DMA_MINALIGN)`.
   - The comment above the `buffer` array has been updated to reflect that DMA may require the transfer buffers to live in their own cache lines, rather than stating it as a requirement.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in the alignment of the `buffer` array is directly related to the need for ensuring DMA safety on platforms with larger cache lines. By switching to `IIO_DMA_MINALIGN`, the patch addresses potential issues with non-coherent DMA operations, thereby improving the reliability of data transfers in the driver. The updated comment provides clarity on the nature of the requirement, indicating that while DMA may require specific alignment, it is not an absolute necessity in all cases. This change enhances the robustness of the driver while also providing better documentation for future reference.
